about: Recall test set: earlier answers and notes from the demo's topics, and questions re-asked in different words. gold = the item a correct recall must return. Written 2026-11-07; extend with real (anonymised) conversations.

turns.q: DO fell below 30 % in batch B-117 on BR-07. What could explain it?
turns.a: Dissolved oxygen slid from 61 % to 24 % over 01:00-04:00 while antifoam dosing escalated; first use of antifoam lot L-8812 is the clearest change; probe calibration and pump maintenance were in order.

turns.q: Could the DO probe itself be the problem?
turns.a: Unlikely: the BR-07 probe passed a two-point calibration and bump test on 30 Oct, and the decline was smooth rather than a step.

turns.q: Forecast viable cell density and glucose for CHO-003-R01 from 72 h.
turns.a: The Monod model projects viable cells rising to about 8.1 million cells/mL by 114.5 h and glucose falling to 2.3 g/L; mean absolute error after the cutoff was 1.09 million cells/mL and 0.46 g/L.

turns.q: Compare viability across the six runs in the September delivery.
turns.a: CHO-003-R02 collapsed between 114.5 h and 142 h (89 % to 6 %) while its sister run stayed healthy; four of six runs ended near zero viability at the last samples.

turns.q: Is the September CMO delivery trustworthy?
turns.a: All 804 source cells were accounted for and every accepted value matched the original file byte for byte; that proves faithful conversion, not that the process was in control.

turns.q: Have we seen foaming on BR-07 before?
turns.a: Yes: DEV-12 in June (worn antifoam pump AF-2 seal, dosing lagged foam onset; seal replaced) and DEV-19 in August (new antifoam lot L-8790, root cause not established).

turns.q: What would QA need to review DEV-31?
turns.a: The QMS record, the DO trend, the antifoam dosing log, the probe calibration and the lot history are on file; missing are product-impact data, the executed SOP record and the L-8812 certificate of analysis.

turns.q: Which open deviations are highest risk, and who owns them?
turns.a: DEV-31 is the only open deviation; you own it with the QA lead as reviewer; it repeats a foaming pattern on BR-07.

turns.q: What would you check before transferring this process to a larger bioreactor?
turns.a: Resolve the foaming and low-oxygen issue on BR-07 first, since foaming worsens at higher superficial gas velocity; characterise run-to-run variability; document agitation and sparge settings.

turns.q: Show glucose in g/L please, not mmol/L.
turns.a: Noted: glucose will be reported in g/L.

turns.q: Which run had the highest lactate?
turns.a: CHO-003-R02 reached 2.707 g/L lactate at 142 h, the delivery maximum, while glucose was not exhausted.

turns.q: What CAPA came out of DEV-12?
turns.a: The AF-2 pump seal was replaced and AF-2 was added to monthly preventive maintenance; no foaming recurred in the next six batches.

notes.text: Antifoam lot L-8812 was first used in B-117; new antifoam lots preceded both DO dips on BR-07 (DEV-19, DEV-31). Check the lot CoA first next time.
The person wants glucose reported in g/L, never mmol/L.
The CHO Monod model under-predicts glucose consumption mid-run (89-95 h); do not trust its glucose forecast for feed timing.
Open thread: the supplier certificate of analysis for lot L-8812 has not been received; follow up before closing DEV-31.
